rounds.text: Nila Infrastructures Ltd is trading at a compelling valuation with a P/E of 11x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 6.86x against a sector benchmark of 22.37x [E11], sitting at a steep discount to broader sector multiples [E6, E7]. The underlying profitability metrics significantly outperform sector benchmarks, highlighted by an ROCE of 20.53% versus a sector benchmark of 3.14% [E10] and an ROE of 12.43% against a sector benchmark of 5.78% [E9]. Growth has been stellar over medium-term horizons, marked by a 5-year compounded profit growth of 124% [E19] and 3-year compounded sales growth of 41% [E16], proving that fundamentals have vastly outpaced recent share price performance [E56]. Furthermore, the balance sheet is exceptionally conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.12x and borrowings decreasing to Rs 24 Cr [E38, E39]. A discounted cash flow model suggests a massive margin of safety of 72.8% [E46], and a reverse DCF indicates that the current market price implies zero earnings growth [E47], completely mispricing the company's strong historical compounding. Conceded: [E34], [E35], [E36], [E63].

Nila Infrastructures Ltd trades at a compelling discount, marked by a low price-to-earnings ratio of 11x against a sector benchmark of 33.03x [E1, E6]. This undervaluation is further underscored by an EV/EBITDA of 6.86x compared to the sector benchmark of 22.37x [E11]. The business demonstrates robust capital efficiency, delivering a ROCE of 20.53% that comfortably outpaces the sector benchmark of 3.14% [E10]. Fundamental momentum has been stellar over medium-term horizons, highlighted by a compounded profit growth of 124% over 5 years and 143% over 3 years [E19, E20]. Operating margins have also expanded to 9% in TTM from 6% three years earlier [E30], while the balance sheet remains conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.12x [E38]. Conceded: [E34, E35, E36] show negative operating and free cash flows alongside weak cash conversion in March 2026.
